has demonstrated strong free cash flow generation and a revitalized focus on inventory expansion under CEO Nick Del'Osso, but stretching the balance sheet into anincreasingly uncertain natural gas macro in 2027 could compound investor inventory concerns with balance sheet discipline questions, according to Jefferies analysts led by John Edelman.
Offsetting the leverage concern is positive hedging, Edelman said, as Gulfport
has locked in roughly one third of its 2027 program at an attractive ~$3.85/Mcf price, and the analyst expects the liquids cut to increase to 10% as the company leans on wet gas inventory.
Separately, Edelman initiated coverage of Comstock Resources
with a Hold rating and $14 price target, saying the company is the most sensitive to changes in front-month natgas prices among stocks in his coverage.

title: Gulfport Energy cut at Jefferies on near-term natural gas price risks
